title: Sterilization vs. Disinfection

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Sterilization eliminates all forms of microbial life, including bacterial endospores. Disinfection reduces pathogenic microorganisms to a safer level but does not reliably kill all endospores.
explanation: These terms describe different endpoints, not different intensities of the same process. A method (e.g. autoclaving) is typically described as achieving sterilization when validated to do so; many chemical disinfectants used on surfaces are effective against vegetative cells but are not sporicidal at the concentrations/contact times typically used for routine disinfection. The correct choice depends on the item, the organism risk, and the intended use (e.g. a surgical instrument requires sterilization; a benchtop after routine work is typically disinfected).

comparison.left: Sterilization: kills/removes all microbial life, including spores
comparison.right: Disinfection: reduces pathogens to a safer level; spores may survive

commonMisconceptions: That 'disinfected' and 'sterile' are interchangeable words for the same outcome.
